items.title: Rudimentary Lathe comes out of retirement for the 3rd time
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I miss when a bunch of us weirdos overshared on our TiddlyWikis nearly every day. Most are gone or unmaintained now. Can we bring them back? I'll start: rudimentarylathe.org

Nearly 5,000 notes going back to 2018, and man oh man, at least 4,800 of them are an embarrassment. I should keep this stuff to myself, but that horse left the barn long ago.

We used to write "TiddlyMails" to each other (I don't think we actually called them that). I'd write a note that simply mentioned someone with their own wiki. They'd read it, and write a note on their wiki with a link back and a title something like: "Re: That thing you wrote". It was completely manual and done without pings or notifications of any kind. So fun!

If you have a similar wiki, let me know. I'd love to visit!

TiddlyWiki is more than 20 years old and still a miracle to me.

items.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
When it comes to note-taking software, I prioritize usefulness over longevity. I prefer plain text (e.g. .org and .md files), I prefer having both, but I'm not going to reject an app that makes my notes useful today, due to some kind of functional "lock-in".

I think I need to teach Claude about TiddlyWiki...and Tinderbox.

items.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I hate to admit this, but I kind of miss Lightroom Classic. It was nice having a very good RAW processor and capable catalog with a large ecosystem and all of my photos in one big library. I've spent so much time trying to concoct a non-Adobe workflow that I've forgotten why I bother. :). Plus, Negative Lab Pro.

Org is the source language, not an inconvenient input to be normalised into markdown.

I'm pretty content with 11ty right now, but how am I not going to at least this?l

items.title: Westenberg on Generative Overload
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Your AI tools can produce a research brief in 45 seconds. A 1,500-word competitor analysis with tags and backlinks, filed in the right folder before you finish your coffee. A full knowledge graph connecting everything you’ve read this month to everything you saved last quarter.

The problem is - you’re not reading any of it.

items.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I need to do something about how or if I continue to participate on Mastodon. The unrelenting flood of discourse around LLM use, although often ethically relevant, is more often intellectually dishonest and exaggerated to the point of silliness. I'm bored by it. Y'all have fun.

I'd buy an iPhone Duo just to run this (via Daring Fireball)

And as I grow, I’m learning to declare fewer absolutes in a complex, imperfect, and constantly changing world.

items.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: Someone on quxnet had their Gemini capsule listed, so I opened Lagrange for the first time in a while. Gemini space is so calm and consistent! On a whim, I set up my own server. It's at . I'm not going to do any sort of HTML-proxying. Everything there is gemtext only.

items.title: Sunday, October 25, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
For the past two days I've automatically reached for quxnet via the CLI (quxterm). I didn't expect this.

I've been wondering about Mastodon, lately. It seems that no matter how I aggressively I cull my feed, it remains saturated with tiresome and repetitive takes and topics that I'm tired of talking about. Going back to Twitter has been A Thing recently, but that's not happening with me. It might just be time for a break.

items.title: Quxnet.net
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Remember when I said that I was done signing up for every new service that comes along? Yeah, me too. But...

Quxnet has everything. Boards, mail, photo galleries, links, blogs, an RSS reader, and more. It looks super-retro cool, which adds to the vibe. I don't know what I want out of it yet, but if it can remain "A private network with old internet manners." then I can see it becoming a fun new place to hang out.

There are still fewer than 1,000 people there, so naturally things are cordial and sufficiently nerdy and polite. I hope it stays polite, but I worry that with popularity comes conflicting views from people who "We" don't agree with, and once the finger-pointing starts, things tend to go south. I hope it doesn't happen that way.

But for now it's clever, fun, nerdy, and new, so I'm in. https://quxnet.net/u/jbaty.

items.title: Discord, or the Death of Lore
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I have no disputes as the popularity of [Discord], the things that happen there, and the unquestioned vivaciousness of being the party that never seems to end and everyone wants to join.

I just happen to be the sort of person who notices there’s no decent fire exits and most of the structure is wood and there’s an… awful lot of pyrotechnics being set off.
